Ready for the maintainer to merge at the next cut. No blocking findings.

The example conditions, guide heights and automatic threading meet issue #3214. Each condition and the machine description identify the examples. The guide gives replacement steps. The tests check posting, replacement of a condition, and taper refusals.

I reviewed this as a safety-tier change because the machine data changes posted output. I checked the six changed files against AGENTS.md at upstream/main 4d6b75e77. No golden files changed. No UI code changed, so screenshots are not required.

Results, run locally in an isolated worktree after a clean trial merge with upstream/main:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: passed. Both selected builds passed.
- Post `machine_tree`: 13 passed.
- Post `ream_lathe`: 7 passed.
- App `probe_no_coolant`: 5 passed.
- App `sodick_alc400g`: 6 passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 8 -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.

Extra suites run:

- App `machine`: 33 passed.
- App `machine_library`: 16 passed.
- App `posting`: 17 passed.
- No fixture or importer changes require the additional kernel suites.

Heavy lane check: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` selected `probe_no_coolant`. That source has no ignored tests. The changed Sodick suite also has no ignored tests. There are no applicable heavy tests. I did not count the dry run as a test pass.

Mutation checks, run locally:

1. Restore the old machine file: RED, with the three failures reported in the PR body.
2. Set `edm.awt` to false: RED. The first-contour test fails because T91 and T90 are absent.
3. Remove EXAMPLE from the condition notes: RED. The example-marker test fails on C110.
4. Restore the PR machine file: GREEN, all six Sodick tests pass. The worktree has no remaining changes.

Requested before merge: none.

Limits: no physical Sodick control was tested. The example values require replacement before cutting. The existing post warns that its control words are unverified and that each condition must exist in the control table. It still refuses tapered output.

The first gate attempt selected unrelated upstream changes before the trial merge was committed locally. I stopped it and ran the corrected quick gate above. No GitHub runner was used.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 6f2c3cc87e7fa437ff6258504e745699b7acc114 -->
Second safety read (Opus, read-only): blockers

Scope: the head `6f2c3cc87` (one commit on top of `main`, no commit of another open PR). The PR is open and not merged. I read the diff, `assets/machines/sodick-alc400g.mch`, `assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps`, `assets/posts/wire-iso.cps`, `crates/app/src/operation/wire_op.rs`, `crates/app/src/posting_wire.rs` and `crates/app/src/machine/wire_edm.rs` at the head. I did not build.

## Blocker

1. **The posted program does not say that its kerf comes from an example gap.**
   - The Wire Contour path is a wire-centre path. The offset is the wire radius plus the condition `gap` (`wire_op.rs`, `condition_of`). The Sodick post writes no G41 / G42 (`sodick-wire.cps:221`, `:272`).
   - With this PR, a user who does not edit the file gets a path with an offset of 0.125 + 0.04 = 0.165 mm. The 0.04 mm gap is an invented value.
   - The posted word `C110` then selects the real row C110 of the control's own table. That row can have a different gap, or it can be for a different wire or height. The part is then the wrong size by the gap difference. Wire EDM tolerances are in microns, so this is a wrong part.
   - Only the condition id goes to the post (`posting_wire.rs:230`, `PARAM EdmCondition`). The name "Rough cut (example)" and the `EXAMPLE` notes never get to the program. The program says only `CONDITION C110 MUST EXIST IN THE CONTROL CONDITION TABLE - CHECK ITS VALUES` (`sodick-wire.cps:318`). The operator cannot compare the control row with the gap that CamCraft used, because the program does not state that gap.
   - Before this PR, the same case was a visible refusal. After this PR, it is a silent post on invented data. This is against the Prime Directive ("correct, or visibly refused with a diagnostic").
   - Recommended fix (small): when a posted condition's `notes` start with `EXAMPLE`, write a program note and a post warning. For example: `CONDITION C110 IS AN EXAMPLE ROW - THE KERF USES AN EXAMPLE GAP OF 0.040 MM - REPLACE IT BEFORE CUTTING`. Also write the gap of each condition in its note, so the operator can compare it with the control row. Pin the note in `a_first_wire_contour_generates_and_posts_on_the_shipped_file`, and pin its absence in `a_punch_posts_through_the_sodick_post_on_it` (user row `C210`).

## Checked, no finding

- Clean room: the values are original, each is marked "EXAMPLE - not a Sodick figure", and the description says the same. No HSMWorks text, post or library is used. No third-party data, so no licence note is necessary.
- Guide heights 0 / 130 mm: they cannot reach posted U / V. The Sodick post refuses every taper (pinned). `wire-iso.cps` refuses this file because it states no `edm.codes` (`wire-iso.cps:143`). The guide-span check (`wire_verify.rs:54-67`) can now refuse work below Z0 or above Z130, but that is a refusal, not a wrong output.
- `awt: true`: on a machine without a threader, T91 / T90 give a control alarm, not a wrong cut. The guide says to set it to `false`. Note: `lower_guide_z` 0 and `awt` have no public source named; the decision file justifies only the 130 mm upper guide.
- Gaps 0.04 / 0.02 / 0.01 mm are smaller than the 0.125 mm wire radius and decrease from rough to finish. They are plausible as examples.
- No other machine, post or golden changes. Only `sodick_alc400g.rs` names this file in tests; `machine.rs:770` reads only its kind.
- The shipped file is loaded and posted in three tests. No new code on a user path; `expect` is in tests only. `sodick_alc400g.rs` has 204 lines.

Coordinator, for @mkinney: the second safety read on head 6f2c3cc87 (comment 7075321111) found one wrong-output blocker.

- The Wire Contour offset is the wire radius plus the condition `gap`. On the shipped Sodick ALC400 file, that gap is an example value (0.04 mm), not a Sodick figure.
- The posted program names only the condition id (`C110`). It does not state the gap that the offset used, and it does not say that the row is an example. If the real control's C110 has a different gap, the part has the wrong size, with no diagnostic.
- Before this PR, the same case was refused. Now it posts on invented data.
- A small fix is enough: when the notes of a condition start with `EXAMPLE`, write a program note and a post warning that give the example gap. Pin this in the shipped-file test.

I added `needs-rework` beside your `merge-ready`. I removed no label. The two collaborators decide on this PR. Please do not merge until the blocker is fixed or the disagreement is settled.

The maintainer said in chat on 2026-11-22: "PR's with merge-ready cannot have needs-rework at the same time.."

This PR had both labels. The second safety read of the current head `6f2c3cc87` (NeoTech, 06:25:48Z) found blockers, and it stands. I removed `merge-ready`. The label `needs-rework` stays. The label `merge-ready` can return when a new head gets a clean review.
